concepts.content: If the domestic interest rate is above the international interest rate, the exchange rate today must be above the expected exchange rate, implying an expected depreciation that compensates for the higher domestic interest rate. Conversely, if the domestic bond pays a lower interest rate, the exchange rate today is very depreciated because an appreciation is expected to offset the interest rate differential.
